question: Does newly indexed text from the official Silliman Journal article provide a waterbody-specific historical fish lead for Paitan Lake, and does it add fish inventory evidence for Vaca Dam Reservoir?

sourceAccess.accessResult: Search-indexed text from the publisher-hosted article PDF exposed selected methods, results, and table excerpts on 2026-11-19. Direct PDF retrieval and PDF screenshot attempts still returned HTTP 502; no local copy or full text was obtained.
sourceAccess.scopeOfReview: Only the retrieved publisher-indexed excerpts were reviewed. The paper's study scope and the prose statement naming Leiopotherapon plumbeus at Paitan Lake are explicit. Table 3's Oreochromis niloticus row and Paitan Lake column are visible in the indexed excerpt. No other row-to-Paitan assignment is made from flattened table text.
sourceAccess.citation: Paz-Alberto, A. M., Castro, E. S., Flores, V. L., & Romero, M. A. V. (2009). Endemic, Indigenous, and Introduced Species in the Freshwater Ecosystems of Nueva Ecija and Pampanga: Status, Diversity, and Impacts. Silliman Journal, 50(2), 43-60.
sourceAccess.dateCaveat: The article page displays a 2022 published field while the issue and article identify the work as Volume 50(2), July-December 2009. The source does not provide a verified field sampling date in the reviewed excerpts.

studyDesignAsReported.stations: Three designated stations per Nueva Ecija study area; ten randomly selected 10 m by 12 m quadrats per station.
studyDesignAsReported.sourceReportedIdentificationProcess: The article says identifications were authenticated by fisheries technologists at CLSU and NFRDI and by a National Museum taxonomist. This report does not independently verify the underlying identifications, vouchers, or specimen-to-station records.

paitanLakeFindings.sourceStatement: The article's discussion specifically names Paitan Lake among the Nueva Ecija sites where this fish was identified.
paitanLakeFindings.sourceReportedStatus: The authors classify it as endemic in the study context; this review does not independently validate geographic status or current presence.
paitanLakeFindings.evidenceLocation: Publisher-indexed article PDF text, discussion around printed pages 55-56; Table 1 also reports site-specific importance values.
paitanLakeFindings.temporalScope: Historical survey; field collection date not verified.
paitanLakeFindings.disposition: Waterbody-specific historical candidate only; no current-presence, abundance, catchability, legal, safety, or season claim.

paitanLakeFindings.sourceStatement: The article lists this introduced fish in Table 3, whose column headings include Paitan Lake; the Paitan cell has a reported value.
paitanLakeFindings.sourceReportedStatus: The authors classify it as introduced in the Nueva Ecija study.
paitanLakeFindings.evidenceLocation: Publisher-indexed article PDF text, Table 3 around printed pages 50-51.
paitanLakeFindings.temporalScope: Historical survey; field collection date not verified.
paitanLakeFindings.disposition: Waterbody-specific historical candidate only; no current-presence, abundance, catchability, legal, safety, or season claim.

unresolvedPaitanEvidence: Other source-reported Nueva Ecija fish names are not assigned to Paitan unless a row-to-column relationship is explicit in the reviewed excerpt.
The flattened indexed text does not reliably map every Table 1 or Table 3 value to a site, so no additional fish are inferred from numeric alignment.

A 2009 news report contains conflicting statements about janitor fish in Paitan, while later national material uses broader Pterygoplichthys genus language. This review does not reconcile species identity or present status.
No exact collection dates, station coordinates, voucher identifiers, current survey, waterbody geometry, or item-specific public reuse permission were verified.

vacaDamReservoir.result: No fish inventory evidence was found for Vaca Dam Reservoir in the Silliman study: its Nueva Ecija study areas include Paitan and Pantabangan, but not Vaca.
vacaDamReservoir.relatedEvidence: The official CLSU 2021 report documents one joint stock-enhancement activity at Paitan Lake and Vaca Dam Reservoir and gives combined counts of Nile tilapia, mudfish, and carp without allocating counts or taxa to either waterbody.
vacaDamReservoir.disposition: Vaca remains a separate waterbody lead with no species-by-waterbody inventory established in this review. Do not transfer Paitan or Pantabangan fish records to it.

rightsAndUse.publisherTerms: The Silliman Journal issue identifies author and journal copyright and all-rights-reserved terms; the reviewed editorial policy requires written permission for reproduction of the article or two or more tables/figures.
rightsAndUse.localRetention: No article PDF, screenshot, full-text copy, table, figure, or numeric SIV values were retained.
rightsAndUse.decision: Retain only attributed, concise name-level findings for internal research triage. Public species pages and projections remain unapproved pending taxonomy, independent locality support, and rights review.

nextStep: Cross-check the two Paitan source strings against a current authoritative taxonomy source, then seek an independent dated Paitan specimen or survey source and item-specific rights guidance. Continue separate Vaca research; keep Central Luzon incomplete.
